title: Collect employee names into an unmodifiable list, and build an id-to-name lookup as an unmodifiable map, using `Collectors.collectingAndThen` to apply a finishing step. Explain how `collectingAndThen` wraps a collector with a final transformation and why it is used for immutability.
shortTitle: Build an immutable lookup map and an unmodifiable list using Collectors.collectingAndThen
keyPoints: `Collectors.collectingAndThen(downstream, finisher)` runs a collector and then applies one final function to its result.
The finisher commonly wraps a mutable collection with `Collections::unmodifiableList` or `Collections::unmodifiableMap`.
It lets you produce a read-only result in a single stream pipeline instead of collecting then wrapping on a separate line.
`unmodifiableList`/`unmodifiableMap` return a view that throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on any modification attempt.
An unmodifiable view still reflects changes if the backing collection is mutated, so avoid keeping a reference to the backing collection.
The finisher can be any transformation, not only immutability, such as wrapping a count into a formatted report.

s1_definition.oneliner: `collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList)` collects the stream into a list and then applies a finishing step that wraps it as read-only, all in one pipeline.
s1_definition.profdef:
`Collectors.collectingAndThen` composes two collectors into one.

- **Downstream collector** – the collector that gathers the stream, such as `toList()` or `toMap(...)`.
- **Finisher function** – a `Function` applied once to the downstream result before it is returned.
- **Single pipeline** – the finishing step runs inside the collect call, so you do not need a separate line to transform the result.
- **Common use** – wrapping the mutable result with `Collections::unmodifiableList` or `Collections::unmodifiableMap` for immutability.

The finisher can perform any final transformation, but immutability is the most frequent reason to reach for it.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, Rajesh prepares a list of account holders for an audit. He writes all the names down (the downstream collector) and then stamps the sheet "FINAL – DO NOT EDIT" before handing it over (the finisher). Once stamped, nobody can add or erase a name; any attempt is rejected. `collectingAndThen` is that two-step routine of gathering first and stamping second, and `unmodifiableList` is the stamp that makes edits bounce back.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Stream<Employee>
        │  map(Employee::getName)
        ▼
  Stream<String>
        │
        │  collect(collectingAndThen(DOWNSTREAM, FINISHER))
        ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │              collectingAndThen                 │
  │                                                │
  │   DOWNSTREAM = toList()                         │
  │      supplier   -> new ArrayList                │
  │      accumulate -> add each name                │
  │      finisher   -> ArrayList [Rajesh, Priya]    │
  │                        │                        │
  │   FINISHER = unmodifiableList                    │
  │                        ▼                        │
  │           read-only List<String>                │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
  add()/remove() ──▶ UnsupportedOperationException
```

```text
  View vs Copy
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ unmodifiableList (a VIEW)     │   │ toUnmodifiableList (a COPY)   │
  │ backing ──┬── view            │   │ source  -->  independent list │
  │ change backing -> view changes│   │ change source -> copy intact  │
  └──────────────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
When Rajesh collects account-holder names for an audit, he does two things: he writes down every name, and then he stamps the sheet "FINAL – DO NOT EDIT" before handing it over. `collectingAndThen` is exactly that two-step routine in code. The first argument is the downstream collector that gathers the data, such as `toList()` or `toMap(...)`. The second argument is a finisher function that runs once on the collected result.

The most common finisher is `Collections::unmodifiableList` or `Collections::unmodifiableMap`, which wraps the mutable result as read-only. The value is that the mutable `ArrayList` or `HashMap` never escapes into the surrounding code. Everything happens inside one collect expression, so no caller gets a chance to mutate the container before it is sealed.

There is a subtlety worth remembering. `Collections.unmodifiable*` returns a view over the original collection, so if you still hold the backing reference and change it, the "read-only" view changes too. For a truly independent result, prefer `List.copyOf` or `Collectors.toUnmodifiableList()`, which make a real copy and reject null elements.

The finisher does not have to be about immutability. It can turn a count into a formatted report, convert a list into an array, or wrap grouped lists so each group is immutable. The pattern is always the same: collect, then finish.

In our banking work the habit is to never hand out a mutable collection you built in a stream. Seal it with `collectingAndThen` so accidental edits bounce back as `UnsupportedOperationException`.

Remember one sentence: `collectingAndThen` runs a collector and then applies a finishing function, most often wrapping the result as unmodifiable so it leaves the pipeline read-only.
